scenes.narration: [serious] A young man in Canada opened strangers' emails for 100 dollars each.
His name was Karim Baratov. He admitted breaking into over 11,000 email accounts.
People paid him to get inside. But one customer, America says, was Russia's spy agency.
That same spy agency was linked to the Yahoo hack of 500 million accounts.
Meanwhile, he drove fancy cars, like an Aston Martin.
In March 2017, police arrested him at home in Canada. Later, he admitted it in a U.S. court.
He got five years in prison. His 100-dollar jobs helped Russian spies, officials said.

facts.claim: Baratov, born in Kazakhstan and living in Hamilton, Ontario, charged $100 per hack, was arrested in Hamilton in March 2017 and pleaded guilty in November; he got five years and a $250,000 fine
Baratov admitted hacking more than 11,000 webmail accounts from 2010 to March 2017 and became a resource for Russia's FSB
The 2014 Yahoo breach affected about 500 million users; Russia's FSB paid Baratov and provided stolen data
Baratov was 22 when charged and owned an Aston Martin
Sentence was handed down in May 2018

seo.title: Karim Baratov: The $100 Hacker Who Worked for Russian Spies
